q: For a gradient system ẋ = −∇V(x) on ℝⁿ, the function V serves as a Lyapunov function. The dynamics has the property that:
opts: dV/dt = −|∇V|² ≤ 0 along orbits, with equality only at equilibria
Orbits spiral around minima of V
exp: Along solutions of ẋ = −∇V: dV/dt = ∇V · ẋ = −|∇V|² ≤ 0. By LaSalle, orbits converge to equilibria (where ∇V = 0). Gradient systems have no periodic orbits—all energy is dissipated monotonically.
